newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina to beat Q1 deficit goal by $150 mln.
newsitem.headline: Argentina to beat Q1 deficit goal by $150 mln.

text.p: Argentina's fiscal deficit in the first quarter is set to be $150 million smaller than the target of $1.04 billion agreed with the International Monetary Fund, Finance Secretary Pablo Guidotti said Friday.
"An IMF mission is revising the targets for the first quarter...surely they will show an improvement, beating the target by $150 million," Guidotti told reporters.
Guidotti said the estimated reduction in the first-quarter deficit had been raised to $150 million from the previous estimate of $33.8 million.

That was because there will be corrections to the preliminary deficit figures for the first three months of the year. In addition, a payment by the treasury to service $131.5 million worth of bonds held by the Central Bank will be considered as having a neutral impact on spending by the IMF.
"This is in line with what we had forecast...but for the second quarter the deficit target is smaller which means we will have to watch the development in revenues closely," he said.
The deficit target for the first half of the year is $1.4 billion and for the whole year $3.0 billion.
